newsitem.title: UK: SHORT STG FUTURES SEEN OVER-OPTIMISTIC ON UK RATES.
newsitem.headline: SHORT STG FUTURES SEEN OVER-OPTIMISTIC ON UK RATES.

text.p: The rally in British interest rate futures following the Bank of England's latest rate rise may be overdone, leaving little value left in the strip, analysts said on Thursday.
The 12 to 16 basis point rise in short sterling futures has left the market discounting just one more quarter point rate rise at most before the peak of the cycle.
This has left investors in the back months of the strip vulnerable to a sell-off should next week dish up any stronger than expected UK data, analysts said.
"Perhaps this has all been initially a bit overdone," said Tom Rayner, gilts analyst at Societe Generale in London. "The interpretation of the Bank of England's comments was very optimistic."
The Bank signalled a quarter point rise in British interest rates on Thursday to 7.0 percent, its fourth hike since May. It also delivered a strong hint that would be the last rise for some time.

"Upward pressures on the exchange rate should be reduced by the perception that interest rates have reached a level consistent with the inflation target," the Bank's new Monetary Policy Committee said.
Interest rate futures took the statement to heart.
By mid afternoon, December short sterling was up 0.13 on the day at 92.68. The March 1998 future was also up 0.13 at 92.67, suggesting interest rates will peak around 7.25 percent early next year.
"I'd be a bit nervous about December and March at these levels," said Rayner.

From there, the strip showed three month money market rates drifting down, with the June 1998 future up 0.15 at 92.71, and the September contract up 0.14 at 92.81. That suggests the market will be starting to think about the possibility of an easing in rates by then.
Rayner said the market may need some evidence to contradict the rosy inflation scenario painted by the Bank to bring it back to earth. And data next week could provide that trigger.
The action packed week includes July retail price data on Tuesday and key unemployment and earnings data on Wednesday.
Marc Ostwald, analyst at The London Bond Broking Company, agreed there was little value left in the strip.

"The back months represent very poor value," he said. "This rally is definitely overdone. Okay, rates are on hold for a couple of months, but there is still a consumer boom on, and there'll be more signs of that feeding through."
He said the Bank of England had been keen to suggest this was the last move for the time being to give a signal to the foreign exchange markets.
"This was a helping hand to Mr Brown on the currency, to try to stop the hot money pouring in," he said.
Neil Williams, chief economist at Sumitomo Finance International in London, said the strength of the UK housing market meant there would be one, maybe two, more rate rises to come.
"Given that real house prices are again strong this year that suggests the risk of GDP sloping off and the UK hitting recession again are looking quite slim," he said.
